Secondary diagnosis: None

Hospital Course:
Ms. Melinda Carson, a 66-year-old female, was admitted on December 16, 2019, primarily for review and management of her chronic Schizophrenia / schizoaffective disorder, which has been stable for approximately 17.4 years under monotherapy with paliperidone. The admission was routine and primarily for monitoring and adjustment of her ongoing psychiatric management.

During hospital stay, Ms. Carson was evaluated by the psychiatric team, including Dr. Alison Allen, a psychiatrist at Turner and Sons Medical Group. Her mental status examination revealed no acute distress, and she was oriented to person, place, and time. She denied any hallucinations, delusions, or suicidal ideation. Her mood was stable, and she exhibited appropriate affect.

Throughout her hospitalization, Ms. Carson's condition remained stable. There were no episodes of acute psychosis or any significant behavioral disturbances. She to receive her home dose of paliperidone 9 mg daily, which she has been on for several years with good effect. No changes were made to her medication regimen during this admission.

Ms. Carson's physical examination, including vital signs, was unremarkable. Her blood pressure was noted to be 125/80 mmHg, and her weight was recorded at 248 pounds. She denied any physical complaints and appeared to be in good general health aside from her psychiatric condition.

An outside lab report from Heritage Diagnostic Services dated April 7, 2013, was reviewed. The results showed a total cholesterol of 299 mg/dL, HDL cholesterol of 59 mg/dL, fructosamine level of 224 umol/L, negative cotinine qualitative test indicating no recent nicotine use, and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) of 49 U/L. These results were consistent with her known health status and did not indicate any acute medical issues requiring intervention during this admission.

Ms. Carson is a former smoker, having quit cigarettes in 2001 after smoking one pack per day since 1974. She reports consuming approximately one alcoholic drink per week. She engages in regular physical activity, running three to four times a week, which is commendable for her overall health maintenance.

Family history is significant for hypertension in her father, who was diagnosed at age 71 and lived to 85

years old.

Discharge Plan:
Ms. Carson was discharged home in stable condition on December 19, 2019. She will continue her current regimen of paliperidone 9 mg daily. She was advised to maintain her regular follow-up appointments with her psychiatrist and primary care physician for ongoing management of her Schizophrenia / schizoaffective disorder and general health monitoring.

Follow-up:
Ms. Carson is scheduled for a follow-up appointment with Dr. Alison Allen in one month to assess her psychiatric status and medication adherence. She was also encouraged to continue her healthy lifestyle practices, including regular exercise and limited alcohol consumption.

Discharge Medications:
- Paliperidone 9 mg daily

Social History:
- Tobacco use: Former smoker, quit in 2001 after smoking one pack per day since 1974.
- Alcohol use: Approximately one drink per week.
- Exercise: Runs three to four times per week.

This discharge summary was prepared by Dr. Alison Allen, Psychiatrist, Turner and Sons Medical Group. If you have any questions or need further information, please contact the office at [contact information].
